title: Theodore the Presbyter on the Genuineness of Dionysius the Areopagite
english: The treatise of Theodore the presbyter has been read by me, arguing that the book of Saint Dionysius is genuine. Four objections are taken up in the treatise: first, that if it were genuine, some of the later Fathers would have recalled its sayings and usages — yet none did; second, that Eusebius, son of Pamphilus, in compiling a register of the books composed by our blessed Fathers, made no mention of it; third, how this book expounds in detail traditions that grew up in the Church by degrees and over long time — for great Dionysius, as the Acts make plain, lived alongside the Apostles, while what the book contains is for the most part a record of traditions that grew up in the Church by degrees or at a later date; it would be implausible, so the objection runs, indeed a fabrication, to hold that Dionysius set down what grew up in the Church long after great Dionysius's death. Fourth, how the book recalls the epistle of God-inspired Ignatius — for Dionysius was at his height in Apostolic times, whereas Ignatius completed his contest through martyrdom under Trajan, writing the epistle the book recalls a little before his death. Having promised to resolve these four difficulties, he maintains that, so far as rests with him, the book is the genuine work of great Dionysius.

added_allusions.reason: Dionysius' apostolic contemporaneity, explicitly appealed to Acts (ὡς ἐκ τῶν Πράξεων φαίνεται); unique locus Acts 17:34

translator_notes: Greek locked from Bekker 1824; Freese 1920 used as PD English reference only — not copied.
Codex 1 of 279; Theodore's treatise on Dionysius the Areopagite genuineness is lost (Pseudo-Dionysius).
